attribution_limitations: The valproate intake is an assumed amount (56 g) inferred by the authors from emptied medication boxes; the actual amount ingested is not established.

The initial valproate concentration is printed as >10389.5 μmol/l (therapeutic range 346.5–693.0 μmol/l), while Figure 1, the patient's valproate concentration course, has a y-axis printed from 0 to 1500 μmol/L. Image content is not a conflict side, so the text value is kept literally as review_only and is not reconciled.
Ammonia is printed as 197 μg/ml with a normal range given in g/dl; the unit mismatch is kept literally and not corrected. Blood alcohol is printed with the unit %0, kept literally.

The sentence reporting 255.4 μmol/l does not name the analyte; it follows the sentence about valproate drug-concentration monitoring, but attribution by adjacency is not literal, so the item is review_only with a neutral label.
The later measurements are described only as decreasing "drug concentrations"; the drug is not named in that sentence, so the label keeps the source term.

Laboratory testing showed very high valproate levels, a detectable blood alcohol concentration, slightly elevated ammonia and uric acid, and otherwise normal values.
